messages:
kevin: quick q — PR #4892 is a tiny churn to metrics exposure defaults (no schema change). Do we treat this as a patch or minor? planning a canary tomorrow during the morning window. https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4892

sophia: patch imo if it's config-only and no public API/clients rely on the default. but what about default routing weights — could affect perf and latency profiles for some customers

maria: it's already behind a feature flag in the PR, so rollout is gated. that argues patch too. but need release notes line: "tweak default telemetry sampling" or similar

alex: minor if it's going to change observable billing/cost estimates for customers. do we have any customers pinned to defaults? pinging @ops-oncall

ops-oncall: we have two internal customers that pinned defaults (not external prod), they're ok with a patch. if it helps, we can notify them in the morning before canary

kevin: fair. main question is tagging convention. do we push a patch tag v1.12.7 with buildmeta (ci+timestamp) or do we prefer v1.12.8~chore? we want the releasebot to auto-publish release notes snippet

release-bot: auto-check: this PR touches infra/config and telemetry-service defaults. No API surface change detected. Suggested semver: patch. Will attach changelog stub if tag created.

maria: i'll take the notes. suggested blurb: "chore(infra): reduce default telemetry sampling to lower storage; gated behind flag". Keep it short in release notes, expand later if customers ask

alex: also confirm rollback plan: canary -> stable after 2h if no regressions. If regressions, revert flag at runtime (feature flag) + rollback tag if necessary. Good?

kevin: yep. question for releasebot behavior: when we tag as patch do we keep buildmeta in the semver (v1.12.7+ci.20260321) or strip it? We rely on buildmeta for tracing in prod sometimes

release-bot: policy: official release tags use plain semver (no buildmeta) on the stable channel. We keep buildmeta in ephemeral canary tags only (e.g., v1.12.7-canary+ci.367). If you need traceability, include the CI commit hash in the release notes; deploy-bot will annotate the rollout with the SHA

deploy-bot: FYI — I'll create a canary release tag: v1.12.7-canary+ci.1765432101 and schedule a canary job for tomorrow 09:00 PT in the morning window. Will post back with job ID

kevin: perfect. one more: should we bump patch now or wait until after the canary passes? I'm leaning to create canary tag now and only push the stable v1.12.7 after the canary autopromote

maria: create canary now. release notes stub can live in the tag. only create stable tag after autopromote. avoids churn in stable history

alex: agreed. operationally, if canary fails we can flip the flag and not touch stable. if we need a hotfix on top we create v1.12.8-hotfix later

ops-oncall: noted — i'll watch the canary. set alert thresholds: error-rate + p99 latency + telemetry payload size spikes. if any hit, i'll pause rollout and create an incident thread

kevin: thanks all. i'll create the canary tag and assign the release notes to @maria. will mention the two internal customers beforehand.

maria: assigned, thanks — I'll draft a short customer note for ops slack and add the release note summary on the tag

release-bot: note attached: "chore(infra): adjust telemetry default sampling (flag-gated). Can be rolled back by toggling feature flag.", reaction :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: job/98321 (09:00 PT). Will post run log in this thread when it starts

kevin: awesome. resolving question: semver decision = patch (canary tag now, stable tag on autopromote). closing here unless regressions show up. :thumbsup:
